rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı renders the objects as drink, gambling, idols, and lots, calls them filthy work of Satan, and urges avoidance for deliverance.
rows.anchor: İçki, kumar, putlar, kısmet çekilen zarlar hep şeytan işi murdar bir şeydir, onun için siz ondan kaçının ki yakayı kurtarasınız

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers should avoid forbidden impurities, just as they had not prohibited wholesome lawful things.
rows.anchor: Ey iman edenler helâl olan tayyibâtı tahrim etmediğiniz gibi haram olan habâisten de iyi sakınınız.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hamr means intoxicating drinks, while meysir means lottery and gambling; Elmalılı directs readers to the earlier discussion in al-Baqara.
rows.anchor: muhakkak hamr, yani müskirât ve meysir, yani piyango ve kumar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Anṣāb are stones erected for worship, along with other idols and graven images.
rows.anchor: ensâb, yani ta‘abbüd için dikilmiş taş vesâir evsân ü asnâm

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Azlām are gambling and lottery implements: sticks, arrows, and dice.
rows.anchor: kumar ve piyango kalemleri, okları, zarları

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rijs is filth that sensible minds find repellent and disgusting.
rows.anchor: iğreneceği pis, murdar bir şeydir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling these things Satan’s work identifies them as the devil’s doing and incitement, warning that their evil is absolute or predominant.
rows.anchor: şerr-i mahz veya gālib olduğuna tenbîhen مِّنْ عَمَلِ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنِ buyurulmuş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı cites a hadith likening the wine drinker to an idol-worshipper, reinforcing the prohibition’s association with idolatry.
rows.anchor: hadîs-i şerîfi medlûlünce putperestlik kabîlinden gösterilmiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command is to shun the impure things themselves, and this abstention is made a means of hoping for success.
rows.anchor: bizzat ‘aynlarından ictinab emredilmiş, sâdisen bu ictinab felâh ümidine bir sebep yapılmıştır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is the third and final revelation in the staged prohibition of intoxicants; the earlier stages were 4:43 and 2:219.
rows.anchor: Bu âyet, müskirâtın men‘u tahrîmi hakkında üçüncü ve son olarak nâzil olan âyettir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı says the verse’s chief aim is to prohibit wine and gambling and establish their religious and worldly harms and burdens while clarifying Satan’s work.
rows.anchor: asıl maksad hamr u meysirin tahrîmi olduğu ihtar ve bunların tahrîmini iktizâ eden dînî, dünyevî mefsedet ve veballerini takrir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Havḍ means plunging into a matter in an amusement-like and excessive manner.
rows.anchor: “Havd”, eğlence tarzında ve aşırı derecede dalmak demektir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He links the instruction to 4:140, whose parallel wording clarifies the general address and the meanings of plunging into the verses and turning away.
rows.anchor: âyeti de (bak) bunun tefsîri olduğundan hitâbın hitâb-ı âm olduğunu, “havd”ın ve “i‘râz”ın mânalarını vâzıhan göstermiştir.

rows.speaker: Haşviyye
rows.claim: Elmalılı rejects the Hashwiyya inference that the verse forbids deep inquiry into theology, argument from evidence, or debate.
rows.anchor: bazı Haşviyye’nin tevehhüm ettiği gibi bundan ilâhiyat mesâilinde ta‘mîk u tetebbu‘un, istidlâl ve münazaranın âyâtullaha dalmaktır diye hurmetini istinbâta kalkışmamalı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even during argument over proof, one should not become so absorbed that one neglects the matter the proof establishes.
rows.anchor: ancak delil ile uğraşırken medlulden tegāfül edecek derecede dalgınlığa da düşmemelidir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mockers and deniers in view include the Meccan Quraysh polytheists.
rows.anchor: ki Mekke’de Kureyş müşrikleri böyle yapıyorlardı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When people exceed bounds by mocking, taunting, denying, or ridiculing the revelations, the believer should withdraw and not sit with them.
rows.anchor: onlardan çekil, yanlarında oturma

rows.speaker: İbn Âmir
rows.claim: Ibn Amir reads the verb in the tafʿīl form; Elmalılı glosses the possibility as Satan occupying the addressee and causing the prohibition to be forgotten.
rows.anchor: İbn Âmir kıraatinde tef‘ilden ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ};يُنسِيَنَّكَ}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The possibility of being made to forget reflects that the address applies generally to every believer; Satan may distract someone until he forgets the instruction.
rows.anchor: her mü’mine âm olması haysiyetiyledir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Once reminded, one must not remain seated with the wrongdoers; their label signals transgression in the meaning of havḍ and extends the prohibition to sitting with wrongdoers generally.
rows.anchor: “Zâlimîn” tâbir olunması “havd” mefhûmunda haddini tecavüz mânası bulunduğunu iş‘âr ve illet-i nehyi ta‘mîm ile ale’l-umûm zâlimlerle beraber oturmanın dahi menhî olduğunu tasrihtir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His rendering says the God-fearing bear none of the mockers’ account, though the encounter serves as a reminder so that the wrongdoers may take heed.
rows.anchor: Gerçi Allah’tan korkanlara onların hesabından bir şey düşmez, velâkin bir ihtar olur, belki sakınırlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His rendering describes God as splitting grains and kernels, bringing life from death and death from life, splitting dawn, making night a resting place, and setting the sun and moon for reckoning.
rows.anchor: Allah o dâneleri, çekirdekleri pörtleten, ölüden diri çıkarır ve diriden ölü çıkaran

rows.speaker: İbn Kesîr, Ebû Amr, Ya‘kūb’dan Revh
rows.claim: For 6:98, the cited readings pronounce mustaqarr in the active-participle form.
rows.anchor: İbn Kesîr, Ebû Amr, Ya‘kūb’dan Revh kıraatinde ism-i fâ‘il sîgasıyla فَمُسْتَقَرٌّۭ okunur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Falq is splitting or cracking; habb is a collective noun for grain, and nawā for kernels, with the former pointing to herb seeds and the latter to tree seeds.
rows.anchor: “Falk”, şakk etmek, çatlatmaktır. “Habb”, habbenin, “nevâ” da çekirdek demek olan “nevât”ın cem‘i makamında ism-i cinstir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because both are plants, he finds it more apt to see nawā as the plant germ inside a grain, analogous to the kernel within a date or grape.
rows.anchor: ot ve ağaç ikisi de nebâtî olduğundan “nevât”ı dânenin içindeki mâye-i nebâtî gibi mülâhaza etmek mânen daha muvâfık olacaktır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He notes nüveyye as a diminutive of nevât and suggests that the French word noyau appears to derive from it.
rows.anchor: “nevât”ın tasgīri olarak “nüveyye” dahi denilir ki, Fransızların “noyau”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A seed develops inner motion and pressure that split it, turning rest into motion and continuity into separation; a shoot rises through the upper crack while roots descend through the lower one.
rows.anchor: Allah o dâne, o çekirdek dâhilinden bir hareket, bir tazyik, bir intac husûle getirir; onu altından üstünden falk eder, çatlatır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fine rootlets can split hard ground and even stone, illustrating the diverse and wondrous powers operating within plants as signs of the Creator’s power.
rows.anchor: sert çuvaldızların, sivri bıçakların nüfuz edemeyeceği derecede sulb olan yerleri ve bazı zaman kaskatı taşları bile çatlatır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He urges readers who want fuller appreciation of this intricacy to study plant anatomy, tissues, and vegetative instincts.
rows.anchor: nebâtâtın teşrîhini, ensâcını, garâiz-i uvziyesini tedkik ve mütalaa etsinler.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The varied structures and traits work together to yield fruit; each mature fruit breaks away and returns to the soil with many seeds for a new generation.
rows.anchor: maksûd-ı aslî olan semere tevellüd eder. Bir habbe veya bir çekirdek yerine kat kat kutular, mahfazalar içinde yüzlercesi meydana gelir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same origin and equal natural conditions still produce diverse forms and traits, proving wise, merciful, freely acting divine governance rather than nature or elements.
rows.anchor: Menşe’ bir ve tabiatın, nücûmun, fusûlün, anâsırın tesirleri şerâiti müsâvî olduğu hâlde bir habbeden, bir çekirdekten bu kadar muhtelif ecsâm

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The power that grows plants from seeds also creates seeds from plants; God brings life from death and death from life, a pattern even more evident and extensive in animals.
rows.anchor: Gerek dâneyi, çekirdeği şaktan nebat ve eşcâr çıkarmak ve gerek bir şaktan dâne, çekirdek halk etmek her iki mânasıyla فَالِقُ ٱلْحَبِّ وَٱلنَّوَىٰ O’dur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question asks how people can turn to worship others or escape God’s rule; no state, whether life or death, plant or animal, earth or sky, darkness or light, lies beyond him.
rows.anchor: O’ndan nasıl çevrilir de başkalarına taparsınız?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After establishing that none escapes God’s power, Elmalılı points to his splitting darkness to bring dawn as further evidence of that power.
rows.anchor: Gerek hayatta olun gerek mematta, gerek hayvanlara karışın gerek otlara, gerek yere geçin gerek göğe çıkın

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fāliq al-iṣbāḥ means splitting the darkness to make dawn and bring out light.
rows.anchor: sabahı çatlatan, zulmetleri yarıp fecr yapan, ziyâyı aksettirip tan attıran O’dur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God makes night a quiet setting for rest, veiling the day’s activity so excitement subsides and fatigue can ease.
rows.anchor: O geceyi seken, dinlenecek, istirahat edecek bir muhît-i sükûn

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He notes that this wording is read by reciters other than Asim, Hamza, Kisa’i, and Khalaf al-Ashir.
rows.anchor: Âsım, Hamza, Kisâî ve Halef-i Âşir’den mâ‘adâsında وَجَعَلَ ٱلَّيْلَ سَكَنًۭا okunur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sun and moon are not agents of day and night but instruments marking reckoning; their movements and the cycles of activity and rest are measured.
rows.anchor: Âyet-i nehâr olan Şems ve âyet-i leyl olan Kamer bunların âmil ve fâ‘ili değil, vâsıta-i hisâbiyeleridir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God determined quantities, created reckoning, and made the sun and moon signs by which people account for their activity and rest, for which they are responsible.
rows.anchor: Allah teâlâ mekādîr ve kemmiyâtı ta‘yîn ü tahsis ederek hesabı da halk etmiş, Şems ve Kamer’i bu hareket ü sükûnun hisâbına birer alâmet yapmıştır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The calibrated order of opposed possibilities and forces reflects the exact measure of the Mighty, All-Knowing God, not chance or a blind nature.
rows.anchor: Ne hesabsız, takdirsiz, gelişigüzel, keyfemettefak oluvermiş bir tesadüftür ne de ne yaptığını bilmeyen kör bir tabiatın ıttırâdıdır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s power is unmatched and independent of nature; worshipping natural, vital, or celestial forces under his authority cannot free anyone from his reckoning.
rows.anchor: u fâtır olan Allah yalnız kādir değil, şerîk ve nazîri yok bir Azîz ü Alîm’dir de.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His rendering says God made the stars a means for finding the way on land and sea and elaborated the signs for people of knowledge.
rows.anchor: karada ve denizde yolu doğrultmanız için size yıldızları sebep kılmıştır. Hakikat ilim ehli olanlar için âyetleri tafsil eyledik

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made the stars for human benefit, not humans for the stars; they are lamps of guidance and signs of mercy, not ruling or managing deities.
rows.anchor: sizi nücum için değil, nücûmu sizin için, sizin intifâ‘ınız

words: لِتَهْتَدُوا۟ بِهَا فِى ظُلُمَٰتِ ٱلْبَرِّ وَٱلْبَحْرِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their indications help people orient their destination, directions, qibla, and both material and spiritual paths through land and sea.
rows.anchor: bunların delâletiyle hedefinizi, cihetlerinizi, kıblenizi, maddî mânevî yolunuzu doğrultasınız

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the signs guide everyone and are stated concisely in many distinct points, their intellectual lessons especially benefit people capable of knowledge.
rows.anchor: bilmek şânından bulunanlar istifade ederler.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The created book is richly detailed across land, sea, earth, heaven, plants, animals, atmosphere, and celestial phenomena, and those capable of science can benefit from it.
rows.anchor: kitab-ı hilkatte, berr ü bahrda, arz u semâda, nebâtât ve hayvânâtta, cevviyyât ve felekiyyâtta o kadar çok tafsîlâtı vardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı urges Muslims to study botany, zoology, calculation, observation, meteorological phenomena, and mathematical astronomy on these principles.
rows.anchor: Müslümanlar bu düsturları esas ittihaz ederek nebâtât, hayvânât, hesab, rasad, âsâr-ı cevviye, hey’et-i riyâziye ilimlerini tahsîle

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He invokes 18:109 to convey that the detailed sciences contained in these signs could not be exhausted even by the sea serving as ink.
rows.anchor: قُل لَّوْ كَانَ ٱلْبَحْرُ مِدَادًۭا لِّكَلِمَٰتِ رَبِّى

words: وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِىٓ أَنشَأَكُم مِّن نَّفْسٍۢ وَٰحِدَةٍۢ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God originated humanity from a single soul, which Elmalılı identifies as Adam, and he directs readers to the beginning of al-Nisa.
rows.anchor: Bir candan, bir Âdem’den neş’et ettirdi, üretti (Sûre-i Nisâ’nın başına bak)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He renders the two as a place of settlement and a place of deposit, noting that they occur in varied forms.
rows.anchor: sonra bir müstekar, bir de müstevda‘var: Çeşit çeşit.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His rendering describes rain bringing out every kind of vegetation, then green growth and stacked grain, hanging date clusters, grape gardens, olives, and pomegranates; it invites observing fruit from first growth to ripeness.
rows.anchor: semâdan bir su indirdi, derken onunla her şeyin nebatını çıkardık. Derken ondan bir yeşillik çıkardık, ondan birbiri üzerine binmiş dâneler çıkarıyoruz.
